learning: Iteration 7 showed that wheel_track is near its useful limit, with oval line loss gone. Mass is the remaining yaw-response lever. Iteration 1 changed mass together with track, so its effect was confounded. This run isolates mass, with a small kd increase as the only controller change.
notes: Mass-only test on the iteration 7 design (0.08 m track, seven sensors at 20 mm, y = 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints), with kd raised to 0.30 to damp the faster yaw response. The race will show whether lower yaw inertia closes the 0.06 m floor gap on the curves.
rationale: Iteration 7 is the best result so far (67.95). Narrowing wheel_track to 0.08 m lifted the oval to 84.1 with zero line losses, and the s-bend and slalom rose modestly. Every track still ends off track with max_error about 0.061-0.066 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m floor. The Builder's intent is to change only mass, from 0.6 to 0.4 kg, which is the contract minimum. Yaw inertia scales with mass, so a lighter body should correct faster for the same wheel difference. I keep the Builder's geometry unchanged so the mass test stays isolated. The controller is the same as iteration 7 except kd rises from 0.25 to 0.30. Slalom steering_oscillation was already 0.161 in iteration 7, and a lighter body responds more quickly, so a little more damping is the main risk to manage. kp, base_speed, the 7-sensor weights and last_direction are unchanged. Expected: max_error on the s-bend and slalom falls toward or below 0.06 m, line_loss_events trend toward 0, and progress rises above the iteration 7 values (s-bend about 0.178, slalom about 0.115). Steering oscillation should stay near or below about 0.17.
